I found one real bug in the uncommitted changes, plus two smaller problems. I read the diff but didn't run the tests or a Fish shell.

1. **Fish completion breaks (`src/click/shell_completion.py:183`).**
   - **Cause:** The patch makes the completer print each completion as three lines (type, value, help). The Fish script then does `string split \n $completion`. But `set -l response (...)` already splits the output into one list item per line. The `for` loop therefore sees `plain`, `--at` and the help text as three separate items. `$metadata[2]` and `$metadata[3]` end up empty, so Fish completion fails for every command.
   - **Fix:** Loop three items at a time, like the zsh script's `for type key descr in`. Alternatively, keep the old one-line format and just escape the newlines.

2. **Help text handling (`src/click/shell_completion.py:436`).**
   - **Sentinel collision:** The code uses the string `_` to mean "no help", so an option whose help text is really `_` loses its description.
   - **Escaped newlines:** Newlines are replaced with a literal `\n`, so Fish shows a visible backslash-n instead of a line break.

3. **Tests miss the bug (`tests/test_shell_completion.py:559`).** The new tests only check the Python output format. They never run the Fish script, so they pass even though the script can't parse the new format.

findings.summary: The Fish script splits each completion on newlines, but Fish's command substitution `set -l response (...)` already splits the output into one list element per line, so each loop iteration sees only a single line of the 3-line record.
findings.failure_scenario:
The completer prints `plain
--at
<help>
`. `$response` becomes [plain, --at, <help>, ...] and the `for completion in $response` loop runs once per line. In each iteration `string split 
 $completion` gives a one-element `$metadata`. `$metadata[1]` is 'plain' on its own, so `$metadata[2]` and `$metadata[3]` are empty. `test $metadata[3] != "_"` then errors, or the loop echoes empty strings. Fish completion therefore breaks for every command. This is the opposite of the intended fix. The fix is to iterate three lines at a time (like the zsh script's `for type key descr in`), or to keep a single-line format and escape the newlines.

findings.summary: Help text equal to the literal string '_' is used as a sentinel for 'no help', so a real help string of '_' is silently dropped. Newlines are also replaced with the literal two characters `\n`, so Fish displays a backslash-n instead of a line break.
findings.failure_scenario: An option with help='_' shows no description. A multi-line help is shown to the user as 'Attachment with explicit mimetype,\n--at image.jpg ...' with visible backslash-n sequences.

findings.summary: The new tests only check the Python output format. They never run the Fish script, so the Fish-side parsing bug above is not caught.
findings.failure_scenario: The tests pass even though the generated Fish function cannot parse the new 3-line format.
